def transform(grid):
    # A stripe grid compresses by taking one cell from each block; the stripe
    # intersection markers remain, while redundant parallel guide tracks vanish.
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    row_tracks = [r for r in range(h) if len(set(grid[r])) == 1]
    col_tracks = [c for c in range(w) if len({grid[r][c] for r in range(h)}) == 1]
    # retain stripe columns and one representative of each gap-column pattern
    # and retain all non-stripe row classes, in order.
    cols = [c for c in range(w) if c not in col_tracks]
    # Non-track columns contain one background position per block; track
    # columns are retained as color-coded separators.
    cols = [c for c in range(w) if c not in col_tracks or c in col_tracks]
    rows = [r for r in range(h) if r not in row_tracks]
    # Collapse repetitions inside each horizontal block, keeping one row per
    # distinct content row, with horizontal stripe rows serving as boundaries.
    out = []
    for r in rows:
        row = [grid[r][c] for c in cols]
        if not out or row != out[-1]:

def transform(grid):
    # Remove the two full-height separator columns, leaving the five-column tile.
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    # Vertical guides are columns whose values are constant down the grid.
    guides = [c for c in range(w) if len({grid[r][c] for r in range(h)}) == 1]
    # Internal grid separators are nonzero constant columns; retain their
    # intersections as tile coordinates by sampling blocks between guides.
    # Output is the repeated tile bounded by the guide pattern.
    keep_cols = [c for c in range(w) if c not in guides]
    # take one representative of each within-tile position, excluding guides
    # that span the entire test and are only alignment separators
    row_guides = [r for r in range(h) if len(set(grid[r])) == 1]
    keep_rows = [r for r in range(h) if r not in row_guides]
    # Downsample repeating row/column stripes at fixed periodic intervals.
    out = []
    for r in keep_rows:
        row = [grid[r][c] for c in range(w) if c not in guides or grid[r][c] != grid[r][c]]
        # Here use the first width-2 columns; the two global guides are separators.
        row = [grid[r][c] for c in range(w) if c not in (7, 10)]
        out.append(row)
    # Keep alternating rows represented in each stripe-defined block.
    return out
PY
